props.gloss_en: the mishnah: women, slaves and minors are exempt from the sukkah
the baraita: 'homeborn' -- this is a homeborn; 'THE homeborn' (Lev 23:42) -- to exclude the women
the baraita: 'ALL the homeborn' -- to include the minors
the Yom Kippur baraita: 'THE homeborn' (Lev 16:29) -- to include homeborn women, who are obligated in the affliction
Rabba: they [the two laws expounded from האזרח] are received halakhot
Rabba: and the Sages leaned them on the verses
sukkah is a time-bound positive mitzva
and women are exempt from every time-bound positive mitzva
Rav Yehuda in Rav's name (and the school of R' Yishmael): 'a man or a woman' (Num 5:6) -- the verse equated woman to man for all punishments in the Torah
Abaye: actually, [women's exemption from] sukkah is the halakha (answering הי קרא והי הלכתא: so the Yom Kippur inclusion is the verse's)
the sukkah verse's 'THE homeborn' is to include converts
the Yom Kippur verse's 'THE homeborn' is needed only [to include women] in the addition to the affliction
